title: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold
plain: The ozone-reducing coating on the radiator is not working as well as it should. It does not affect how the car drives.
symptoms: No change in how the car drives

causes.name: Radiator replaced with one that lacks the special coating
Coating worn or dirty
Faulty monitoring sensor

checks: Check whether the radiator has been replaced with an aftermarket part
Check for other ozone catalyst sensor codes
fix: Usually a radiator with the correct factory coating.

title: Turbocharger Speed Sensor Circuit
plain: The computer is watching the turbocharger speed sensor and has spotted an electrical fault. It measures how fast the turbo is spinning so the computer can control boost safely.

causes.name: Unplugged, loose or corroded connector at the turbocharger speed sensor
Broken or chafed wire in the turbocharger speed sensor circuit
Failed turbocharger speed sensor
Missing reference voltage or ground from the computer
Control module fault (rare)

checks: Look over the connector and wiring for the turbocharger speed sensor, checking for damage, corrosion or a loose fit
Check power, ground and signal with a meter
Clear the code and see if it comes back
fix: Repair the wiring or connector if it is damaged; otherwise replace the turbocharger speed sensor.

title: Turbocharger Speed Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
plain: The computer is watching the turbocharger speed sensor and is getting a signal that does not make sense for current conditions. It measures how fast the turbo is spinning so the computer can control boost safely.

causes.name: Failing or sticking turbocharger speed sensor
A real problem in the system the part works with
Wiring or connector with high resistance
Computer software that needs an update

checks: Check for other codes that point to the underlying problem
Compare the turbocharger speed sensor reading with expected values in live data
Inspect the wiring and connector
fix: Find out whether the turbocharger speed sensor itself or the system it works with is at fault, then repair or replace as needed.

title: Vacuum Reservoir Control Circuit/Open
plain: The computer is watching the vacuum reservoir control circuit and sees what looks like a broken or disconnected circuit. This valve manages stored engine vacuum used by the brake booster or other systems.
symptoms: Brake pedal may feel harder than normal

causes.name: Unplugged, loose or corroded connector at the vacuum reservoir control valve
Broken or chafed wire in the vacuum reservoir control circuit
Failed vacuum reservoir control valve
Blown fuse or failed relay feeding the circuit
Control module fault (rare)

checks: Look over the connector and wiring for the vacuum reservoir control circuit, checking for damage, corrosion or a loose fit
Check power, ground and resistance of the part with a meter
Clear the code and see if it comes back
fix: Repair the wiring or connector if it is damaged; otherwise replace the vacuum reservoir control valve.

title: Vacuum Reservoir Control Circuit Low
plain: The computer is watching the vacuum reservoir control circuit and is reading a voltage that is lower than it should be, which often means a short to ground or a failed part. This valve manages stored engine vacuum used by the brake booster or other systems.
symptoms: Brake pedal may feel harder than normal

causes.name: Control wire to the vacuum reservoir control valve shorted to ground
Failed vacuum reservoir control valve
Corroded or loose connector
Control module fault (rare)

checks: Inspect the wiring in the vacuum reservoir control circuit for rubbed-through insulation touching metal
Check the wiring for a short to ground with a meter
Clear the code and see if it returns right away
fix: Fix any shorted wiring first; if the wiring tests good, replace the vacuum reservoir control valve.

title: Vacuum Reservoir Control Circuit High
plain: The computer is watching the vacuum reservoir control circuit and is reading a voltage that is higher than it should be, which often means a broken ground or a short to power. This valve manages stored engine vacuum used by the brake booster or other systems.
symptoms: Brake pedal may feel harder than normal

causes.name: Control wire to the vacuum reservoir control valve shorted to voltage or the part open inside
Failed vacuum reservoir control valve
Corroded or loose connector
Control module fault (rare)

checks: Inspect the wiring and ground connection for the vacuum reservoir control circuit
Check for wires melted or rubbed together in the harness
Measure the circuit with a meter before replacing parts
fix: Repair the open ground or shorted wire; if the wiring is fine, replace the vacuum reservoir control valve.

causes.name: Hood switch dirty, misadjusted or damaged
Failing or sticking hood switch
A real problem in the system the part works with
Wiring or connector with high resistance
Computer software that needs an update

checks: Check for other codes that point to the underlying problem
Compare the hood switch reading with expected values in live data

fix: Find out whether the hood switch itself or the system it works with is at fault, then repair or replace as needed.

title: Turbocharger Speed Sensor Circuit Low

Failed turbocharger speed sensor
Corroded or loose connector
Control module fault (rare)

checks: Inspect the wiring in the turbocharger speed sensor for rubbed-through insulation touching metal
Unplug the turbocharger speed sensor and see if the reading changes
Clear the code and see if it returns right away
fix: Fix any shorted wiring first; if the wiring tests good, replace the turbocharger speed sensor.

title: Turbocharger Speed Sensor Circuit Intermittent
plain: The computer is watching the turbocharger speed sensor and is seeing a signal that cuts in and out. It measures how fast the turbo is spinning so the computer can control boost safely.

causes.name: Loose connector or chafed wire that loses contact over bumps
Turbocharger speed sensor failing on and off
Corrosion inside the connector
Poor ground connection

checks: Wiggle the wiring for the turbocharger speed sensor with the engine running while watching live data
Check connector pins for corrosion or spread terminals
Note when it happens (hot, cold, bumps) to narrow it down
fix: Repair the loose or corroded connection; replace the turbocharger speed sensor if the wiring is solid.

title: Cruise Control Front Distance Range Sensor Single Sensor or Center
plain: The computer is watching the adaptive cruise front distance sensor and is getting a signal that does not make sense for current conditions. This radar or camera sensor measures the distance to the car ahead for adaptive cruise control.
symptoms: Adaptive cruise or collision warning may not work

causes.name: Sensor blocked by dirt, snow or ice
Sensor knocked out of alignment
Failing or sticking adaptive cruise front distance sensor
Front bumper or grille damage, or a non-original grille or emblem in front of the sensor
Wiring or connector with high resistance

checks: Check for other codes that point to the underlying problem
Compare the adaptive cruise front distance sensor reading with expected values in live data
Inspect the wiring and connector
fix: Clean the sensor, check for damage, and have it aimed (calibrated); replace it if it has failed.

title: Fuel Additive Control Module Requested MIL Illumination
plain: The module that adds a cleaning fluid to diesel fuel found a fault and asked for the check engine light.

causes.name: Fuel additive tank low or empty
Fault stored in the fuel additive module
Additive pump or wiring problem

checks: Scan the fuel additive module for its own codes
Check the additive fluid level
fix: Refill the additive and repair the fault stored in the additive module.

title: Fuel Additive Control Module Warning Lamp Request
plain: The diesel fuel additive module is asking for a warning light, usually because the additive is low or its system has a fault.

causes.name: Fuel additive fluid low
Fault stored in the fuel additive module
Additive pump or wiring problem

checks: Check the additive fluid level
Scan the fuel additive module for codes
fix: Refill the additive and fix any stored additive system fault.

title: PTO Enable Switch Performance
plain: The switch that turns on the power take-off (used on work trucks to run equipment) is not acting as expected.

causes.name: Faulty PTO switch
Wiring or connector fault
PTO control module fault

checks: Inspect the PTO switch and wiring
Watch the switch signal in live data while operating it
fix: Repair the wiring or replace the PTO switch.

title: Torque Management Request Output Signal
plain: The engine computer sends a signal that tells other modules how much engine power to allow, and that signal has a fault.
symptoms: Harsh shifts or reduced power possible

causes.name: Wiring or network fault between modules
Engine or transmission computer needing a software update
Control module fault

checks: Check for network or transmission codes
Inspect wiring between the engine and transmission computers
fix: Repair the wiring or update the module software as directed by the maker.
